papers.title: Therapeutic acute intermittent hypoxia does not alter whole-brain cerebrovascular function in healthy individuals
papers.abstract: Acute intermittent hypoxia (AIH) therapy is a promising intervention known to elicit beneficial neuroplasticity. It has been suggested that AIH may also modulate cerebrovascular function, yet the cerebrovascular effects of specific therapeutic intermittent hypoxia protocols remain poorly characterized. Understanding whether AIH results in favorable or adverse cerebrovascular changes is critical in establishing the safety of AIH treatments in populations with elevated cerebrovascular risk. This study investigated cerebral blood flow, cerebrovascular reactivity to hypoxia, and blood pressure effects in a sham-controlled crossover trial (NCT05164705). Healthy young adults (n=18) completed three-week arms of AIH (12 sessions, 15 cycles of 60 seconds hypoxia alternated with 60 seconds normoxia) and sham (6 sessions, normoxia) treatments; phase-contrast and arterial spin labeling magnetic resonance imaging were used to quantify whole-brain and regional cerebral blood flow and hypoxic cerebrovascular reactivity. Blood pressure was measured acutely (before and after each intervention session) and longitudinally (before and after 3 weeks of treatment). AIH treatment did not significantly alter whole-brain resting cerebral blood flow or cerebrovascular reactivity to hypoxia. Blood pressure was unaffected by the treatment acutely or longitudinally. Voxel-wise analysis identified modest regional perfusion increases in the frontal pole, postcentral gyri, and precentral gyri with AIH relative to sham. Significant variability between subjects and between sessions in the hypoxic burden delivered with this AIH protocol was also identified. Overall, this three-week therapeutic AIH protocol produced minimal sustained hemodynamic changes in healthy young adults. The insights from this trial lay a foundation for safely expanding access to this promising rehabilitative intervention in clinical populations.

papers.title: Proteomics of steady-state and culture-derived human erythropoiesis reveals the dynamics of erythroid stress
papers.abstract: To generate a mature red blood cell, erythropoiesis requires the committed erythroid progenitor cell and later erythroblast stages to undergo a continuum of extreme morphological and functional remodeling. In vitro culture has been crucial to understand the extensive proteome dynamics that underlie this process. However, the millions of cells required for conventional proteomics technologies preclude the study of erythropoiesis within the steady-state human bone marrow (BM). Thus, culture-induced stress may shape our understanding of erythroid maturation. To address this knowledge gap, we developed an optimized methodology for low-cell proteomics (pauciproteomics) and pursued total proteomic analysis of paired steady-state BM and culture-derived erythroid precursor stages from 11 healthy donors. This approach defines four main protein expression patterns during BM erythroid maturation which are only partially recapitulated by cultured cells. Culture-induced stress rewires the erythroid proteome from early stages of differentiation, reshaping major transcription factor networks, kinase pathways, metabolic enzymes and erythrokine regulation. Notably, single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of steady-state healthy and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) BM demonstrates that the cultured cell proteome parallels gene expression dynamics within the MDS BM, modelling the regulation of in vivo stress erythropoiesis. Culture-specific alterations were mostly restricted to extensive carbonic anhydrase dysregulation and embryofetal globin switching, both potentially linked to altered gas exchange dynamics in culture. In conclusion, we reveal the steady-state erythroid proteome and its substantial remodeling by culture-induced stress, reframing existing knowledge on erythroid differentiation, defining new elements of stress erythropoiesis and guiding future studies in the field.

papers.title: Endothelial CXCL12 is dispensable for adipose tissue function
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The adipose tissue endothelium plays a critical role for tissue function in acting as an interface between circulating blood and the various tissue-resident cells. Proper endothelial function ensures, among other things, well-regulated adipose tissue lipid in- and efflux, immune cell diapedesis, and oxygen supply. Dysregulated lipid flux, inflammation, and adipose tissue hypoxia are hallmarks of adipose tissue dysfunction and metaflammation. Additionally, lipid uptake and oxygen supply are important processes enabling heat production in active brown adipose tissue (BAT), which is associated with cardiometabolic health in humans. However, so far, little is known about the role of adipose tissue endothelial cells (ECs) and their intercellular communication with other adipose tissue cell compartments. Particularly, how this communication changes during thermogenic stimuli such as cold exposure is largely unknown. Methods: We used transcriptome analysis of adipose tissue ECs to identify EC Cxcl12 as a potential regulator of adipose tissue function. In vitro experiments were performed on primary sympathetic neurons and immortalized ECs. The role of EC Cxcl12 in adipose tissue function was analyzed in vivo using conditional knock-out mice. Results: Cxcl12 expression was induced in BAT ECs upon exposure to cold. Recombinant CXCL12 increased axon outgrowth in primary sympathetic neurons and angiogenesis in ECs. Conditional knock-out of Cxcl12 in ECs did not yield a discernable phenotype in mice either in normal housing or during cold adaption. Additionally, we could show that EC-derived CXCL12 does not play a role in adipose tissue dysfunction during obesity. Conclusions: Cxcl12 is highly expressed in the adipose tissue endothelium, but appears to be dispensable for adipose tissue function.

papers.title: Increases in therapist-patient physiological synchrony after dog-patient contact in canine-assisted psychotherapy: an exploratory pilot study
papers.abstract: Introduction: Canine-assisted psychotherapy (CAP) introduces a therapy dog into the therapist-patient relationship and may influence interpersonal processes underlying therapeutic change. This exploratory pilot study investigated whether direct patient-dog contact is associated with changes in autonomic arousal and therapist-patient physiological synchrony. Methods: Skin conductance was recorded from 18 patients with depressive disorders and one therapist during 53 routine CAP sessions. A total of 192 episodes of direct patient-dog contact were identified from video recordings. Three-minute periods before and after each contact onsets were compared. Skin conductance level (SCL), skin conductance fluctuations (SCF), and therapist-patient physiological synchrony were assessed using zero-lag correlation and maximum cross-correlation. Sliding-window analyses examined temporal changes in synchrony, while randomly selected pseudo-events served as controls. Results: SCL increased significantly following dog contact in both patients and the therapist, whereas SCF rate over 3 min did not change significantly. Therapist-patient physiological synchrony increased significantly after dog contact, as indicated by both zero-lag correlation and maximum cross-correlation. Sliding-window analyses confirmed these increases and showed a reduction in the temporal lag between the two physiological signals. Importantly, increases in synchrony were significantly greater following genuine dog-contact events than following pseudo-events. Discussion: Direct physical contact between patients and therapy dogs is followed by increased autonomic arousal and enhanced therapist-patient physiological synchrony. These findings suggest that dog-patient contact may function as an interactional event that promotes physiological coordination and interpersonal attunement within the therapeutic dyad.

papers.title: RNA-seq analysis of Triatoma gerstaeckeri during mite infestation reveals increased metabolic demand and lower reproductive investment
papers.abstract: Triatomine insects, also known as kissing bugs, serve as vectors for the Trypanosoma cruzi parasite, which can cause American trypanosomiasis, also known as Chagas disease. Triatomines are known to be parasitized by mites in natural and colony settings, where mites feed on the arthropod to obtain nutrients and resources for reproduction. This feeding, while necessary for the survival of the mites, likely occurs at the expense of their insect host. We examined the transcriptional response of Triatoma gerstaeckeri infested with mites (Pimeliaphilus spp.) and an uninfested group using Illumina-based RNA-seq, followed by targeted measurement of nutritional reserves in both groups. Our results show increased expression of factors involved in protein translation, but decreased expression of processes associated with cell development. These results are supported by declines in protein levels in mite-infested T. gerstaeckeri and lower expression of reproductive factors, suggesting a distinct reduction in nutrient reserves and reproductive output. These studies provide critical information on the interaction of mites and triatomines while considering the utility of mites as biological control of triatomines in nature or for husbandry protocols to minimize issues with mite infestations of colony individuals.

papers.title: Cardiometabolic stress induces atrial myopathy in mice, characterized by structural remodelling, metabolic dysfunction, and incomplete transcriptional recovery.
papers.abstract: Background: The mechanisms underlying atrial remodelling and recovery following the withdrawal of cardiometabolic stress remain incompletely understood. We investigated the functional, metabolic, and transcriptional consequences of metabolic-hypertensive stress (MHS), a murine model of cardiometabolic HFpEF, in the left atrium (LA) and assessed the reversibility of these alterations following myocardial recovery. Methods and Results: Male and female mice underwent a two-hit HFpEF-inducing protocol consisting of angiotensin II infusion and a high-fat diet combined with physical inactivity (metabolic-hypertensive stress, MHS). Following 4 weeks of MHS, mice underwent a 4-week myocardial recovery (MR) phase involving stress withdrawal, dietary normalization, and voluntary exercise. We assessed LA function by speckle-tracking echocardiography, mitochondrial respiration by high-resolution respirometry, and transcriptomic remodelling by bulk RNA sequencing. MHS markedly reduced LA reservoir, conduit, and contractile strain, consistent with atrial myopathy. Transcriptomic analyses revealed substantially greater remodelling in the LA than previously observed in the left ventricle under comparable experimental conditions. Hallmark pathway analysis showed activation of extracellular matrix remodelling and profibrotic signalling pathways, along with suppression of oxidative phosphorylation and fatty acid metabolism. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified a structural remodelling module enriched for extracellular matrix organization and angiogenesis pathways, as well as a bioenergetic module enriched for mitochondrial respiratory functions. Although inflammatory and structural remodelling pathways largely normalized following myocardial recovery, mitochondrial and metabolic programs exhibited incomplete restoration. Persistent transcriptional alterations were concentrated within a stress-responsive gene network enriched for adaptive cellular response pathways. In parallel, a discrete regulatory module displayed significant sex-dependent expression patterns. Conclusions: Metabolic-hypertensive stress induces profound atrial functional, metabolic, and transcriptomic remodelling, consistent with the development of cardiometabolic atrial myopathy. While many stress-induced changes resolve following myocardial recovery, key bioenergetic and stress-responsive transcriptional programs persist, suggesting that cardiometabolic stress leaves a lasting molecular imprint within the atrium.

papers.title: Hepatocyte UBE4A protects against MASLD/MASH by maintaining ER homeostasis via UBXN4 interaction
papers.abstract: Molecular understanding of the regulation of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) functions in healthy and MASLD livers is limited. Here, we elucidate that Ube4A, a cytosolic E3 ubiquitin ligase, protects against MASLD development by maintaining ER homeostasis during nutritional stress. Hepatocyte-Ube4A deletion (HUKO) augments Gubra-Amylin-diet (GAN-D)-induced steatosis, inflammation, insulin resistance, ER stress and markers of steatohepatitis of the liver in both sexes of mice. Proteomic studies reveal that in addition to altered metabolic and fibrogenic pathways, levels of many ER proteins are also changed in HUKO livers. Impaired ER functions sensitize HUKO livers to nutrition- or chemical (tunicamycin)-induced ER stress. Moreover, HUKO primary hepatocytes exhibit increased ER stress. Furthermore, Ube4A maintains ER homeostasis by facilitating ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD). The lipogenic protein SCD1 is identified as one of the ERAD targets of Ube4A. SCD1 stability and triglyceride accumulation are amplified in HUKO primary hepatocytes. The liver Ube4A-interactome studies identified the ERAD mediator UBXN4 as a major Ube4A interacting protein. Alphafold3-based molecular modelling and interaction site mapping analyses pinpointed the Ube4A binding residues for UBXN4. ER-localized Ube4A-UBXN4 complex facilitates ERAD (e.g., SCD1) and UBXN4-binding deficient Ube4A mutants fail to enhance this process. Finally, Ube4A and UBXN4 are downregulated in the livers of human MASLD and MASH patients and this complex is diminished in GAN-D-fed mouse livers. In conclusion, Ube4A preserves ER homeostasis by maintaining ERAD via its interaction with UBXN4, which maintains liver health. Enhancing levels and/or preserving interaction of these proteins may offer new therapeutic strategies for MASLD treatment.

papers.title: THE MULTIFUNCTIONAL PROTEIN E4F1 REGULATES MELANOCYTIC FUNCTIONS IN MICE THROUGH PROTEIN TRANSLATION AND MITF EXPRESSION
papers.abstract: The multifunctional protein E4 transcription factor 1 (E4F1) is an essential regulator of skin homeostasis, playing a critical role in epidermal stem cell maintenance and keratinocyte differentiation. However, the functions of E4F1 in other skin cell type remain poorly investigated. Here, we describe its role in melanogenesis, the physiological process for synthesis of melanin pigments. Using genetically engineered mouse models that enabled conditional inactivation of E4f1 specifically in melanocytes, we demonstrated that E4f1 loss induces severe pigmentation defects without affecting melanocyte survival nor differentiation. At the molecular level, E4f1 depletion reduces the expression of its direct transcriptional target genes involved in protein translation, including Elp3 and Eef1g, leading to translation alterations and consequently the induction of the Integrated Stress Response (ISR). This response resulted in microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF) downregulation, inducing a decrease in the expression of enzymes involved in melanin synthesis. Consistent with these findings, Elp3 or Eef1g depletion recapitulated the decrease in MITF levels in vitro, and pharmacological inhibition of ISR partially rescued melanin content in vivo, confirming a key role of the E4F1-protein translation-ISR cascade in melanogenesis. Together, our data identify E4F1-associated translation functions as a key regulator of the melanocytic lineage.

papers.title: BCKDK Inhibitors Directly Antagonize Angiotensin II Type 1 Receptor and Induce Vasodilation Independently of BCAA Catabolism or BCKDK
papers.abstract: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA) have been implicated in diabetes and heart failure, leading to ongoing clinical trials with inhibitors of BCKDK, a key regulator of BCAA catabolism. We have previously shown that these inhibitors promote vasodilation and lower blood pressure, well-known cardioprotective effects, but how this occurs remained unclear. We show here, using explanted vessels, in vivo hemodynamics and telemetry, and genetically modified mice, that the vasodilatory effect of BCKDK inhibitors is direct, rapid, independent of nitric oxide, independent of BCAA catabolism, and most strikingly, independent of BCKDK itself. Instead, we demonstrate, using structural and biochemical studies, that BCKDK inhibitors directly antagonize the angiotensin II type I receptor (AT1R) and consequent angiotensin-mediated vasoconstriction. These data demonstrate a strong off-target effect of BCKDK inhibitors, independent of BCAA or BCKDK, which may explain their cardioprotective effects but also questions if this protection would be additive to existing AT1R blockers.

papers.title: The constitutive androstane receptor protects against metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease through sex specific interactions with the gut microbiota
papers.abstract: Background: The gut-liver axis is involved in Metabolic dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD), but the host molecular actors involved in such dialogue have not yet been fully characterized. Objective: We investigated the sex-dependent role of the Constitutive Androstane Receptor (CAR) as a hepatic sensor of microbial signals in MASLD pathophysiology. Design: Male and female Car+/+ and Car-/- mice were fed a western diet (WD) for 4, 14 or 35 weeks. We performed plasma biochemistry, liver histology, bile acid and cholesterol quantification, untargeted multi-omics approach combining liver RNA-sequencing and 16S rRNA sequencing, together with co-housing, fecal microbiota transplantation and analysis of publicly available transcriptomics data in human cohorts. Results: Short-term WD revealed CAR-dependent protection against steatosis, together with perturbations in the transcriptional signatures of multiple transcription factors involved in hepatocyte identity in males. After 14 weeks, CAR deletion increased WD-induced liver damage, inflammation and fibrosis, and disrupted bile acid, cholesterol and gut microbiota homeostasis, in males only. Co-housing and fecal microbiota transplantations revealed that a Car+/+ gut microbiota protected against WD-induced liver damage, while a Car-/- microbiota was reshaped by a Car+/+ host. No CAR-dependent phenotype was observed in females. Finally, in human cohorts, hepatic CAR expression decreased in advanced clinical stages of MASLD. Conclusion: CAR is a sex-dependent protective nuclear receptor against MASLD progression, acting both as a transcriptional regulator of hepatocyte identity and as a mediator of the host-microbiota crosstalk.

papers.title: Maternal hyperglycemia impairs postnatal skeletal muscle growth and induces stage-dependent gene expression changes in mouse offspring
papers.abstract: Maternal hyperglycemia can affect offspring development and metabolism, but how its effects on skeletal muscle change during postnatal life remains unclear. We investigated skeletal muscle phenotypes in male offspring of streptozotocin-induced hyperglycemic mice at 4 and 8 weeks of age, representing early post-weaning and later postnatal stages, respectively. Maternal hyperglycemia resulted in lower offspring body and skeletal muscle weights at both time points. Myofiber cross-sectional area was reduced without a reduction in total myofiber number, indicating impaired myofiber growth rather than myofiber loss. At 4 weeks, skeletal muscle showed type I/IIA hybrid myofibers and increased expression of fetal, myogenic, and proliferation-associated genes. This immature profile was not maintained at 8 weeks; instead, the transcriptional profile shifted toward reduced mitochondrial and oxidative metabolism. DNA methylation changes at 4 weeks showed limited correspondence with transcriptional alterations. Taken together, maternal hyperglycemia impaired postnatal myofiber growth at both time points, with distinct molecular profiles at 4 and 8 weeks.

papers.title: Cardiomyocyte Perm1 sustains cardiac bioenergetic reserve and exercise capacity
papers.abstract: Objective: Mitochondrial oxidative capacity in striated muscle is governed by the PGC-1/ERR transcriptional axis, which controls not only steady-state respiration but the capacity to expand energy production when demand rises. Whether this reserve function requires dedicated downstream effectors, and whether its loss is detectable at rest, remains unclear. We asked whether Perm1, a striated muscle-specific PGC-1/ERR-induced regulator, is required cell-autonomously for cardiac bioenergetic reserve. Methods: We generated cardiomyocyte-specific Perm1 knockout mice using alphaMHC-nCre, complemented by an adult tamoxifen-inducible alphaMHC-MerCreMer model, and assessed cardiac development, structure, and function longitudinally through 12 months of age in both sexes. We evaluated mitochondrial function by high-resolution respirometry, transmission electron microscopy, and molecular profiling. We tested energetic capacity under load by treadmill exercise with tissue ATP quantification and by beta-adrenergic stimulation of cultured neonatal cardiomyocytes. Results: Perm1 deletion did not perturb embryonic cardiac development, and neither constitutive nor adult-onset deletion impaired cardiac structure, systolic function, or diastolic function through 12 months. Despite this preserved resting phenotype, mitochondrial respiration was reduced by 20 - 25% across complex I- and complex I+II-supported conditions, without changes in citrate synthase activity, mtDNA copy number, or OXPHOS subunit abundance. Instead, the MICOS components IMMT (MIC60) and CHCHD3 (MIC19) were selectively reduced, and mitochondrial subpopulations shifted toward fewer subsarcolemmal and more interfibrillar mitochondria, with unchanged total mitochondrial density. Functionally, Perm1-deficient mice of both sexes showed reduced treadmill capacity at 6 and 12 months and failed to maintain cardiac ATP during exercise at a submaximal workload, while skeletal muscle ATP and plasma lactate were unaffected. This deficit was cardiomyocyte-autonomous: beta-adrenergic stimulation increased ATP content in control cardiomyocytes, but Perm1 knockdown reduced this response. Conclusions. Perm1 is a cardiomyocyte-intrinsic determinant of bioenergetic reserve, dispensable for resting cardiac function but required to expand ATP production under increased demand. These findings identify a mode of metabolic regulation that is invisible to resting functional phenotyping.

papers.title: ENDOMETRIAL GLANDULAR EPITHELIAL CELL PLASTICITY DURING POSTPARTUM REGENERATION AND ESTROUS CYCLICITY
papers.abstract: Several different mechanisms of regeneration have been proposed to explain repair of the endometrial luminal epithelium (LE) following menstrual/estrous cyclicity, parturition or other damaging insults to the uterine mucosa. These include activity of an as-yet unidentified epithelial stem cell population, mesenchymal transdifferentiation, or integration of bone marrow-derived cells. Here, we used a novel Cag-Flox-STOP-Flox-Pgrmc2-3XFlag (Pgrmc2-3XFlag) reporter mouse coupled with a recently developed GE-specific cre recombinase mouse (Prss29-Cre) to determine if and to what extent the GE contributes to regeneration of the LE following parturition and during aging in nulliparous mice. To initiate regeneration in the endometrium, control (Pgrmc2-3XFlag) and reporter (Prss29-Cre;Pgrmc2-3XFlag) mice were placed with males for one pregnancy. Postpartum (pp) uterine tissues were then collected 5 days (1x5dpp), 3-weeks (1x3wpp) and 7-weeks (1x7wpp) later. A fourth set of uterine tissues was collected 3-weeks after three pregnancies (3x3wpp). The number of glands did not change at any time point. Indelibly marked FLAG+ GE cells were detected by immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence in GE as expected. As demonstrated in serial uterine sections of uteri from all four treatment groups, GE cells migrated toward the LE and formed junctional points (JP) where GE cells transitioned from cuboidal GE cells to pseudostratified columnar LE cells. Transitioning cells at junctional points expressed markers of both GE (i.e., FOXA2) and LE (i.e., CALB1) tissues. Following transition, GE-derived LE cells expressed PGR and ESR1 consistent with surrounding developmentally-derived LE cells. About 17 FLAG+ LE cell islands were also observed in 1x5dpp 4 mm longitudinal sections at sites distant from GE-LE junctional points. Interestingly, the number of islands did not change from 1x5dpp to 1x7wpp. However, the total number of GE-derived FLAG+ LE cells observed in each island decreased from 1x5dpp to 1x3wpp, but then tended (p=0.07) to increase by 1x7wpp. There was no difference in the number of GE-LE junctional points or GE-derived FLAG+ LE islands between 1x3wpp and 3x3wpp tissues. However, a significant increase in the total (p=0.02) and average (p=0.02) number of FLAG+ LE cells was observed in 3x3wpp LE islands highlighting the proliferative expansion of these cells over the intervening ~80 days. GE-LE junctional points were also observed in 5-month old nulliparous Prss29-Cre;Pgrmc2-3XFlag mice at diestrus, but not in younger 6-week old mice. Collectively, these findings establish the GE as a quantifiable cellular source for LE regeneration during postpartum involution and as part of normal LE cell turnover during the estrous cycle in nulliparous mice. We propose a mechanism whereby GE cells within glandular structures are not terminally differentiated, but rather are stably differentiated to perform glandular function. However, when needed and based on the level of endometrial damage, GE cells can dedifferentiate, become integrated in to LE tissue and then reprogram to take on an LE phenotype as part of the regenerative process following parturition and during estrous cyclicity over time.

papers.title: Associations between multivariate profiles, lifestyle behaviors and reaction time performance in active young adults
papers.abstract: Lifestyle behaviors influence cardiometabolic and cognitive health through multiple interconnected processes, involving metabolic, cardiovascular, behavioral and cognitive factors. This study aimed to assess associations between multivariate plasma and physiological profiles, and behavioral parameters, and their potential association with reaction time (RT) in active young adults. Data on physical activity levels were collected from wearable devices and GPAQ questionnaire, along with anthropometric and clinical assessments, cognitive tests, and blood analyses. Principal component analysis was performed separately for physiological and plasma parameters, retaining the first two principal components (PCs) from each analysis. Multiple linear regression models were used to evaluate the associations between plasma, sex, physical activity levels (METs), daily step count, and alcohol/marijuana use on physiological PC1/PC2 scores, as well as RT. Continuous independent variables were previously categorized, and combined variables were created to represent specific combinations between plasma/physiological PC1 categories and sex. Physiological PC1 (blood pressure) was associated with combined plasma PC1 (insulin/HOMA-IR)-sex variable, total METs and alcohol consumption (adjusted R2 = 0.30). Physiological PC2 (handgrip strength) was mainly explained by combined plasma PC1-sex variable (adjusted R2 = 0.54), with minimal contribution from behavioral factors. RT was associated with physiological PC1 variable and sex (adjusted R2 = 0.35), with slower responses observed among women with lower physiological PC1 scores or hypotension; these associations were supported by RT-physiological PC1 and RT-blood pressure correlations. These exploratory findings suggest sex-dependent associations between physiological, metabolic and lifestyle-related factors, supporting a holistic approach in future research, particularly among young adults.

papers.title: Oral administration of Angiotensin-(1-7) included in hydroxypropyl β-cyclodextrin attenuates cardiac hypertrophy and inflammation in a mouse model of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: Background Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TTC) is a stress-induced cardiomyopathy characterized by acute cardiac dysfunction, inflammation, and hypertrophy, yet no therapy directly targets the underlying myocardial injury. Clinical studies have reported elevated circulating Angiotensin II (Ang II) levels in TTC patients, suggesting dysregulation of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS). Given the established cardioprotective effects of Angiotensin-(1-7) [Ang-(1-7)] in other cardiovascular diseases, we hypothesized that oral administration of Ang-(1-7) could attenuate acute cardiac remodeling during TTC. Methods Female C57BL/6J mice were subjected to a single high-dose isoproterenol (ISO) injection (300 mg/Kg, intraperitoneal) to induce TTC and received daily oral treatment with Ang-(1-7) complexed with hydroxypropyl {beta}-cyclodextrin [Ang-(1-7)-CD] or vehicle (CD), for 4 days, beginning one day before ISO administration. Cardiac proteome alterations were characterized by tandem mass tag (TMT)-based quantitative proteomics. Cardiac hypertrophy was assessed by heart weight normalized to tibial length and cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area. Myocardial inflammation was evaluated by histopathology, CD68 immunostaining, and flow cytometric analysis of infiltrating leukocyte populations. Results We observed a distinct cardiac proteome signature in Ang-(1-7)-treated ISO mice, predicting inhibition of pathways associated with cardiac hypertrophy and adverse remodeling. These molecular changes were accompanied by reduced heart weight normalized to tibial length and smaller cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area compared with vehicle-treated ISO mice. Oral Ang-(1-7) also attenuated myocardial inflammation, as evidenced by lower inflammatory scores, reduced CD68+ macrophage infiltration, decreased numbers of CD45+ leukocytes, and marked suppression of Ly6G+ neutrophil and CCR2+ monocyte recruitment to the heart. These protective effects were associated with improved survival following ISO challenge. MS data are available via ProteomeXchange (PXD082872). Conclusions Oral administration of Ang-(1-7) attenuated acute cardiac hypertrophy and inflammation in experimental TTC while inducing cardiac proteome changes consistent with reduced adverse remodeling. These findings identify activation of the protective RAS axis as a promising therapeutic strategy for limiting myocardial injury during TTC.

papers.title: Multidimensional Electroglottographic Characterization of Immediate Responses to Straw Phonation: A Pilot Methodological Study in Singers
papers.abstract: Semi-occluded vocal tract (SOVT) exercises are widely used in voice training and therapy, but their immediate electroglottographic (EGG) effects remain incompletely characterized. In this pilot methodological study, six female community singers completed a no-straw baseline recording and then 1-min straw-phonation exercises with four straws (Household metal, Metal VoiceStraw, plastic, and paper), each followed by a no-straw EGG recording. Thirty 1s recordings were analyzed with a standardized pipeline including contact quotient (CQ), waveform skewness, contact-phase rise/fall timing, temporal skewness (s_t), a normalized derivative asymmetry index (NDAI), average-cycle morphology, and EGG spectral descriptors. Relative to baseline, group-mean CQ was higher after all four straws (by 0.027-0.058), waveform skewness and NDAI were lower, and the EGG spectral centroid was lower (by 9.6-15.3%). Contact-phase timing asymmetry did not change consistently: s_t exceeded baseline after three straws and fell below it after one, and the rise/fall ratio decreased in three to five of six participants depending on the straw. Four participants ranked the Metal VoiceStraw first and two ranked paper first. Because every straw condition followed the baseline, warm-up and order effects cannot be separated from straw effects. These hypothesis-generating results identify CQ, waveform skewness, and EGG spectral centroid as candidate endpoints for a larger controlled study

papers.title: Adipose Tissue Pericellular Fibrosis, Weight Loss and Features of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease after Bariatric Surgery
papers.abstract: Introduction: Adipose tissue fibrosis has been associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and suboptimal weight loss after bariatric surgery. The objective was to characterize changes in adipose tissue fibrosis and extracellular matrix (ECM) components in adipose tissues from two abdominal fat compartments, subcutaneous and omental, in response to bariatric surgery; and determine the effect of weight loss on the association between adipose tissue fibrosis and MASLD feature changes with weight loss. Methods: Liver and adipose tissue biopsy samples were obtained before and after weight loss from patients who underwent two-stage bariatric surgery. Adipose tissue pericellular fibrosis was evaluated histologically with picrosirius red staining for collagen quantification and normalized to adipocyte count per microscope field. Transcript levels of ECM remodeling and inflammatory genes were measured by RNA sequencing in subcutaneous adipose tissue pre- and post-surgery. Results: At baseline, adipose tissue pericellular fibrosis did not associate with MASLD features, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis or hepatic fibrosis in patients with severe obesity. Changes in liver histology after surgery were unrelated to changes in adipose tissue fibrosis. Transcripts for most genes involved in ECM remodeling and inflammation were downregulated in subcutaneous fat one year after bariatric surgery. Omental, but not subcutaneous, adipose tissue fibrosis decreased after surgery when adjusted for cell number (mean {+/-} SD: 0.41 {+/-} 0.12 vs 0.32 {+/-} 0.08 {micro}m2/cell, p<0.005). Higher subcutaneous adipose tissue fibrosis correlated with reduced weight loss (estimate {+/-} SE: -2.04 {+/-} 0.99, p<0.05) and BMI loss (-0.73 {+/-} 0.35, p<0.05), while increased omental adipose tissue fibrosis after weight loss was associated with worsening hepatic fibrosis (0.31 {+/-} 0.14, p<0.05). Conclusion: In individuals with severe obesity undergoing bariatric surgery, adipose tissue fibrosis is poorly correlated with MASLD features. Notably, pericellular fibrosis in subcutaneous abdominal, but not omental, adipose tissue was associated with a reduced weight-loss response to surgery.

papers.title: Distinct iron metabolism regulation during cachexia progression in murine models of intestinal and pancreatic cancer
papers.abstract: Background. Cancer cachexia is a multifactorial syndrome characterized by substantial metabolic disturbances including systemic inflammation, and muscle atrophy, which may affect the regulation of iron metabolism in patients. This study aimed to characterize this regulation in two murine models of colorectal and pancreatic cancer, both associated with a high prevalence of cachexia. Methods. Histological, biochemical and molecular analyses were performed in serum, skeletal muscle, liver, spleen and tumor from UN-KC-6141 pancreatic tumor bearing mice and from ApcMin/+ mice (colorectal cancer model), both models exhibiting variable cachexia severity. Results. Both models induce cachexia, but diverge markedly in their regulation of iron metabolism. UNKC mice display reduced plasma iron availability (-9.6% transferrin saturation, p<0.001) without concomitant anemia, while hepatic hepcidin synthesis is upregulated (+100.6%, p<0.001) by inflammation, promoting ferroportin (FPN) downregulation (-42.4%, p<0.001) and iron sequestration in the spleen (+134% total iron content, p<0.001). In the atrophied gastrocnemius, iron concentration is preserved through increased ferritin (+86.6%, p=0.010) and hemoproteins (i.e., myoglobin, CYSC, COXIV) expression. Conversely, ApcMin/+ mice exhibit anemia together with hepatic and splenic iron depletion (-48.4%, p<0.001 and -84.9%, p<0.001, respectively). Hepcidin synthesis is downregulated (-99.9%, p<0.001) despite persistent inflammation, indicating that hypoxia and/or iron-deficiency signals probably predominate over the inflammatory pathway. FPN is markedly decreased (-94.2%, p<0.001) in the iron-depleted spleen despite low hepcidin. In the atrophied quadriceps of ApcMin/+ mice, iron deficiency is associated with decreased FPN and ferritin (-87.9%, p<0.001, and -38.4%, p=0.016, respectively), and increased TfR1 expression (+305%, p=0.107). Finally, tumor iron import may play a significant role in cachexia progression, as suggested by the association between tumor weight, tumor TfR1 protein levels and body weight loss in UNKC mice. Conclusion. These findings reveal cancer type-specific signatures of iron regulation in cachexia, which appear to be more driven by cancer type specific features than by cachexia severity itself, with skeletal muscle iron metabolism impaired mainly when cachexia is associated with anemia. This suggests that the clinical management of iron metabolism in cachectic patients should be guided by the underlying cancer type.

papers.title: Extracellular GPX3 drives insulin receptor expression in adipose tissue independent of its peroxidase activity
papers.abstract: Obesity-associated insulin resistance is driven in part by adipose tissue dysfunction and oxidative stress, yet the role of extracellular mechanisms in modulating insulin signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we show that extracellular Glutathione Peroxidase 3 (GPX3) enhances adipocyte insulin sensitivity and functionalities independent of its canonical peroxidase function. GPX3, a secreted selenoprotein highly expressed in white adipose tissue (WAT), is suppressed in obesity, but whether it actively regulates insulin sensitivity had not been established. We find that WAT GPX3 expression closely mirrors insulin receptor (InsR) expression across a broad range of metabolic parameters in humans and increases dynamically following weight loss. Prolonged therapeutic selenium supplementation in diet-induced obese mice selectively suppressed epididymal WAT oxidative damage, restored GPX3 and InsR expression, and enhanced insulin-stimulated AKT phosphorylation, improving oral glucose tolerance. Mechanistically, recombinant GPX3 extracellularly administered at physiological concentrations induced InsR expression across multiple adipocyte models, including pre-adipocytes, epididymal WAT explants, and adipocyte organoids, by promoting binding of the transcription factor Specificity Protein 1 (SP1) to the Insr promoter, while knockdown of GPX3 completely blocks SVF adipogenesis. These effects rely on the structural integrity, rather than selenocysteine-dependent activity. Thus, we identify a GPX3-SP1-InsR signaling axis in adipose tissue insulin sensitivity, suggesting GPX3 is a novel paracrine mediator of metabolic health and a potential therapeutic target to reinstate WAT insulin sensitivity in obesity and type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: CADENCE: Open-source software for signal conditioning, feature extraction, visualization and analysis of cardiac optical mapping data
papers.abstract: Optical mapping is a fundamental tool for cardiac electrophysiology research. Processing of these signals can be non-trivial, requiring multiple pre- and post-processing steps to limit interpretation errors. Existing software packages have features siloed across platforms and require users to combine several packages for in-depth analysis. To address this, we developed CADENCE, an open-source MATLAB-based application combining feature breadth (e.g., SVD denoising, conduction velocity, alternans, annotated rotors) and depth (e.g., 15 independent alternans features across both voltage and calcium modalities) in an end-to-end pipeline including data conversion, signal conditioning, feature extraction, and signal analysis. We demonstrate CADENCE's capabilities across datasets spanning four species (rat, rabbit, pig, and human), three tissue preparations (slices, wedge, and whole heart), and three camera configurations (single, dual, and panoramic). CADENCE was validated against three blinded expert observers (15 hearts) and demonstrated agreement comparable to inter-observer variability (SD ratios 1.07/0.95/0.89 for APD80, activation, CaTD80). Dominant frequency was recovered with a median error of 0.03% across 84 of 88 paced recordings with 1:1 capture. CADENCE's code is publicly available and distributed as a compiled standalone application that the end-user can install and run without a MATLAB license to encourage adoption and standardization across laboratories.

papers.title: PKA disrupts adult ovarian identity circuits through direct inhibition of TRIM28-chromatin binding
papers.abstract: Functional ovarian plasticity depends on the granulosa cell (GC) fate determination, differentiation, oocyte support and steroid production. After birth, GC identity must be maintained in differentiating follicles, while from puberty, ovarian plasticity is cyclically challenged by gonadotropic hormones. TRIM28-FOXL2 interactions form a key chromatin component maintaining ovarian identity programs and repressing testis-specific genes. This TRIM28 role depends on its E3-SUMO-ligase activity, suggesting SUMOylation in GC can be regulated by transient hormonal cues, although hormonal involvement in modulating GC identity remains to be established. Here, we demonstrated the in vivo interplay between gonadotropic-PKA-signaling and hypo-SUMOylation waves underlying ovarian GC plasticity. In vitro TRIM28 mutagenesis and phospho-proteomics demonstrated direct PKA inhibitory control on TRIM28. This prompted us to highlight SUMOylation alterations in Carney Complex ovarian lesions resulting from chronic PKA activity from rare genetic mutations. Using mutant models, transcriptomics and TRIM28/FOXL2-ChIP-Seq analyses, we specified the in vivo PKA inhibitory mechanisms on TRIM28/FOXL2 chromatin binding and its consequences on adult ovarian somatic cell identity. Together, our data support an integrative model where gonadotrophin pulses create transient windows of PKA-mediated TRIM28 phosphorylation, hypo-SUMOylation, and FOXL2-TRIM28 destabilization. This positions SUMOylation dynamics as central integrator of hormonal signaling and epigenetic identity maintenance in the ovary.

papers.title: Nav1.5 regulates intrinsic cardiac neuronal excitability and expands the cellular basis of SCN5A channelopathies
papers.abstract: Background: Loss- and gain-of-function variants in SCN5A, encoding the cardiac sodium channel Nav1.5, are major causes of inherited cardiac channelopathies. Their pathophysiology has almost exclusively been attributed to altered cardiomyocyte excitability and cardiac conduction. However, growing evidence indicates that autonomic dysfunction contributes to these disorders, raising the possibility that Nav1.5 dysfunction may also affect the intrinsic cardiac nervous system. Objectives: We investigated whether Nav1.5 is functionally expressed in murine intrinsic cardiac neurons and evaluated its contribution to neuronal excitability. Methods: Scn5a expression was investigated by digital PCR and immunocytochemistry in isolated murine intracardiac neurons. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings were used to characterize sodium currents and action potential properties in wild-type and Scn5a+/- mice. Results: Scn5a transcripts and Nav1.5 protein were detected in intrinsic cardiac neurons. Voltage-clamp recordings identified a tetrodotoxin-resistant sodium current accounting for approximately 8% of the total sodium current and displaying pharmacological and biophysical properties consistent with Nav1.5. Activation and inactivation analyses indicated that Nav1.5 is the predominant sodium conductance available at most polarized membrane potentials. Accordingly, Scn5a haploinsufficiency selectively altered action potential threshold, maximal upstroke velocity, overshoot and duration in neurons resting below -60 mV, whereas more depolarized neurons were essentially unaffected. No structural or neurochemical remodeling of intrinsic cardiac ganglia was detected. Conclusion: Nav1.5 is a functional determinant of intrinsic cardiac neuronal excitability. These findings identify the intrinsic cardiac nervous system as a new cellular target of SCN5A dysfunction and suggest that inherited cardiac sodium channelopathies could involve alterations in both myocardial and intrinsic neuronal electrophysiology.

papers.title: PFKFB3 inhibition restores β-cell responsiveness to acetylcholine in a 3xTg-AD pancreatic tissue-slice mode
papers.abstract: The glycolytic regulator PFKFB3 supports dysfunctional {beta}-cell states, but its role in pancreatic Ca2+ signaling remains unclear. We examined responses to PFKFB3 inhibitors (AZ67, AZ26) in pancreatic tissue slices from aged 3xTg-AD mice, a model of Alzheimer's disease that develops impaired glucose tolerance and diabetes as comorbidity. Compared to wild-type controls, {beta}-cells showed weaker glucose-stimulated and acetylcholine-potentiated Ca2+ activity, accompanied by increased nuclear PFKFB3 positivity in insulin-defined islet-cell populations, used here as a PFKFB3-associated stress-state marker. During glucose and acetylcholine stimulation, AZ67 increased {beta}-cell Ca2+ event frequency while maintaining short events. In neighboring acinar cells, PFKFB3 inhibitor exposure was followed by renewed oscillations after acetylcholine-evoked activity had waned. {beta}-cell recruitment was preserved during adrenergic inhibition, and enhanced activity persisted after inhibitor withdrawal, although these recordings were exploratory and residual tissue drug exposure could not be excluded. An effect that survives both drug removal and adrenergic opposition identifies a Ca2+ signaling phenotype in 3xTg-AD {beta}-cells that is acutely inducible yet not transient, and establishes PFKFB3 as a regulator of muscarinic responsiveness in the stressed {beta}-cell.

papers.title: Impaired glycolysis in bone underlies age-related bone loss in mice
papers.abstract: Bone loss and metabolic dysregulation often coexist in older adults, yet the relationship between age-related changes in bone cell metabolism and bone-forming activity remains unclear. By modeling both conditions in aged mice and using in vivo stable-isotope tracing, we demonstrated that age-related decline in bone formation was coupled with an intrinsic impairment of glycolysis within bone tissue. Impaired glycolysis was associated with reduced protein levels of key glycolysis enzymes, and transcriptomics analyses revealed compensatory upregulation of glycolysis genes in aged bone. Metabolic intervention through long-term caloric restriction prevented age-related trabecular bone loss. Furthermore, osteoblast-specific genetic enhancement of glycolysis, via overexpression of HIF1 or the rate-limiting enzyme PFKFB3, significantly improved osteoblast function and increased bone mass in aged mice. Together, the study identifies glycolytic decline as a cell-autonomous driver of osteoblast deficiency and provides proof of principle that reactivating glycolysis can promote bone accrual in aging.

papers.title: Molecular anatomy of the glomerular filtration barrier reveals topology-encoded albumin sieving
papers.abstract: The kidney filters plasma rapidly while retaining albumin, yet where and how this selectivity is encoded within the glomerular filtration barrier remain unresolved. Here we combine cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) of vitrified mouse glomeruli with structure-resolved transport modelling to predict albumin passage from the native three-dimensional architecture of the barrier. Among the three barrier layers, endothelial fenestrae and the flexible Nephrin-Neph1 slit-diaphragm lattice are substantially permeable to albumin. The glomerular basement membrane (GBM) instead provides the dominant restriction through steric exclusion governed by void-network topology. In local GBM reconstructions, water traverses broadly connected void space, whereas narrow throats exclude albumin, leaving few accessible paths. To scale this mechanism to the tissue level, we combine structural statistics from local cryo-ET volumes with mesoscale measurements of GBM heterogeneity to generate representative ensembles. Integrating these ensembles with other layers predicts whole-barrier albumin sieving in close agreement with an independent measurement. The topology-driven mechanism also explains early filtration failure in Alport syndrome mice, in which collagen-IV disruption remodels the GBM network and opens albumin-accessible paths while cellular interfaces remain preserved. These findings identify the structural origin of glomerular albumin selectivity and establish a quantitative route from locally resolved architecture to tissue-scale physiology.

papers.title: Contraction type dependence of serial sarcomere addition following resistance training
papers.abstract: Longitudinal muscle growth occurs through the addition of sarcomeres in series, a process termed serial sarcomerogenesis. To investigate contraction mode dependence of sarcomerogenesis in Sprague-Dawley rats (n=36, 14 to18 weeks, ~468g), we compared the effects of isometric, eccentric, and concentric training (4 to 6 weeks; 3 times/week) on morphological and mechanical adaptations of the plantar flexors. Isometric training was performed at a joint angle corresponding to the plateau nearing the descending limb of the force length relationship, eccentric contractions began at a shorter muscle length and lengthened to this same joint position, and concentric contractions started at this lengthened position but then actively shortened. Owing to the rapid regulation of serial sarcomere number the 4-and 6-week timepoints were collapsed. While force output increased across all training modes (+16%; p 0.05). Therefore, these findings identify the mechanical loading environment associated with isometric and eccentric training as a key driver of serial sarcomerogenesis.

papers.title: Vocal fold injury alters acoustic phenotype despite preserved vocal activity
papers.abstract: Vocal communication depends on the biomechanical integrity of the vocal folds, yet how impairment alters vocal behavior remains poorly understood. We used the California mouse (Peromyscus californicus), a highly vocal species that produces songs through airflow-induced vocal fold vibration, to experimentally examine how defined vocal fold injury alters vocal production. Longitudinal recordings were combined with histological assessment to track changes in vocal function after impairment. Injury produced acute edema of the lamina propria and thyroarytenoid muscle. Despite stable levels of vocal activity, the vocal phenotype shifted characteristically following injury. Thus, vocal behavior can persist despite substantial alteration of the biomechanical tissues underlying sound production, demonstrating that maintenance of behavioral output does not necessarily indicate preservation of the physiological system that generates it. More broadly, these findings establish an experimental link between vocal fold injury and vocal phenotype and provide a framework for understanding how tissue damage and remodeling can reshape acoustic communication even when vocal behavior is maintained. Because repeated vocalization can impose substantial mechanical demands on vocal folds, this framework may have broad relevance for understanding how vocal use, injury, and tissue remodeling interact to shape vocal communication.

papers.title: Multi-scale electrophysiological characterization of human cardioids reveals progressive maturation
papers.abstract: Background: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes are valuable for cardiac disease modelling and drug testing but remain limited by immature structural and electrophysiological properties in conventional two-dimensional cultures. Three-dimensional cardiac models, including cardioids, provide a more physiological environment through multicellular organization and enable tissue-level functional analysis. Their electrophysiological properties and maturation, however, remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We performed an integrated electrophysiological characterization of human cardioids over the first three weeks of maturation using sharp microelectrode recordings, calcium transient measurements, whole-cell patch clamp recordings, immunofluorescence, transcriptomic analysis, and pharmacological interventions. Results: During maturation, cardioids exhibited progressive electrophysiological maturation, characterized by more physiological resting membrane potentials (-54.0{+/-}3.1mV to -68.1{+/-}1.2mV), increased action potential amplitude (73.5{+/-}4.8mV to 101.7{+/-}2.1mV) and upstroke velocity (44.3{+/-}5mV/ms to 86.6{+/-}8.4mV/ms), and shorter action potential duration (178.9{+/-}8.7ms to 144.0{+/-}4.8ms at 1Hz stimulation). These changes were associated with progressively increased INa density and enhanced SCN5A mRNA and Nav1.5 protein expression, consistent with progressive maturation of cardiac excitability. IKr current and KCNH2/hERG expression were already present at early maturation stages and remained stable, as evidenced by preserved sensitivity to dofetilide-blockade. Pharmacological inhibition of barium- and HMR-sensitive currents altered resting membrane and/or action potential characteristics in intact cardioids, whereas in isolated cardiomyocytes classical IK1 remained undetectable and IKs was small, highlighting a certain degree of persisting immaturity of the model. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate that human cardioids undergo progressive electrophysiological maturation and provide complementary tissue- and cellular-level insights into cardiac function, establishing their suitability for investigating INa and IKr-related cardiac pathologies.

papers.title: There is an 'I' in team: Intrapersonal physiological synchrony complements interpersonal physiological synchrony in team interaction
papers.abstract: Interpersonal physiological synchrony (IPS) between interaction partners has been studied as a marker of social connectedness and coordination. However, little is known about how such interpersonal synchrony relates to the intrapersonal coordination of individuals' own autonomic systems during team interaction. The present study examined whether IPS and intrapersonal physiological synchrony (IAPS), defined as the within-person coordination of heart rate (HR), respiration, and electrodermal activity (EDA), function as competing or complementary regulatory processes. It also examined whether IAPS is state- or trait-like and whether teams high or low in both IPS and IAPS had better outcomes. Fifty five newly formed triads (N = 165; Mage = 23.87, 77% female) participated in a laboratory interaction including passive shared experiences and active collaborative tasks while continuous physiological activity was recorded. Synchrony within individuals and between team members was quantified using multidimensional recurrence quantification analysis. Across interaction segments, IAPS was positively associated with IPS in both HR and EDA, with stronger and more consistent associations during active teamwork versus during passive social contexts. These findings contradict a trade-off hypothesis and instead support a synergistic relationship between IAPS and IPS. IAPS exhibited state-like dynamics and sensitivity to features of the context, i.e., consistency within similar interaction contexts and higher in passive versus active social segments. Further, IAPS had limited associations with individual difference measures. Exploratory analyses indicated that teams characterized by both high IAPS and high IPS demonstrated more favorable outcomes, reflected in either higher objective task performance or greater perceived team efficacy depending on physiological modality. Together, these results suggest that effective team coordination is supported not only by IPS but also by the capacity to maintain coherent internal autonomic organization. They further highlight IAPS as a dynamic component of social functioning that merits exploration alongside interpersonal processes.

papers.title: LIPC-E97G Gain-of-function variant potentiates the hypocholesterolemic and anti-atherogenic effects of evinacumab in Ldlr-/- mice
papers.abstract: Introduction: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide (Dagenais et al. 2020), and its main risk factor is LDL-C (Hagenbeek et al. 2020). Only a few genes are associated with LDL-C concentrations, and only 2 genes, ANGPTL3 (Musunuru et al. 2010) and LIPC, are associated with familial combined hypocholesterolemia. Our team recently identified the second genetic cause associated with familial combined hypocholesterolemia, a gain-of-function mutant of the LIPC gene encoding hepatic lipase (HL), LIPC-E97G (Dijk et al. 2022). Although the mode of action of this variant remains largely unknown, we have demonstrated that it significantly increases the phospholipase activity of HL and affects lipoprotein metabolism by promoting plasma cholesterol clearance, particularly of LDL and HDL. Objective: The aim of this study was to explore the additive effect of our HL-E97G variant with a pharmacological inhibitor of the ANGPTL3 protein, evinacumab, on cholesterolemia and atherosclerosis. Materiel and methods: Atherosclerosis measurements were performed on Ldlr-/- mice fed a pro-atherogenic diet. These mice received a single injection of a liver-targeting AAV8 expressing the wild-type or E97G human form of the LIPC gene (1.10E11 genome copies/mouse) and a weekly injection of NaCl or evinacumab (25 mg/kg/week). Results: From a therapeutic approach, we demonstrated a cumulative effect of HL-E97G with evinacumab. Atherosclerotic lesions in the aortic arch of Ldlr-/- mice were reduced by 36% (p=0.4897) with evinacumab, by 65% (p-value=0.0028) with HL-E97G, and by 80% (p-value < 0.0001) with the combined therapy. Conclusion: Our data demonstrate that HL-E97G reduces the development of atherosclerosis in mice in an LDLR- and ANGPTL3-independent manner, strongly reinforcing the therapeutic potential of HL-E97G for patients at high risk of cardiovascular disease.
